title: Nur wir zwei
desc: Four hours, and you will remember three things
setting: A flat mountain top, a path you can walk side by side, and nobody else along.

steps.speaker: Selina
steps.es: Was war dein erster Tag hier?
steps.en: What was your first day here like?

options.es: Vierzig Minuten am Flughafen ohne ein Wort.
options.en: Forty minutes at the airport without a word.
options.feedback: One concrete thing, not a summary. She asked for a day, so give her a day.
True and closed. Two adjectives are a lid, and she was opening something.
You do. It is the first question anybody has asked you that is not woher or seit wann.

steps.speaker: Selina
steps.es: Ich mag den Nebel lieber als die Sonne.
steps.en: I like fog better than sun.

options.feedback: One word, and you get ten minutes. Asking back is the whole skill here.
It is, and she knows. She said it because it is odd, and now she has to defend it.
You do not. Agreeing with something you have not thought about closes it faster than disagreeing.

steps.speaker: Selina
steps.es: Sollen wir noch eine Runde laufen?
steps.en: Shall we walk round once more?

options.feedback: One word. This is a mountain path, not a table: you walk side by side and you do not have to look at each other.
Honest. It is also the end of the afternoon, and she will not offer twice.
She asked what you want. Handing it back is the one answer with nothing in it.
Schön is a big word here. Matching it exactly is the answer; going bigger would put it back down.
A day, with no mal in it. That is the whole move and it is braver than it looks.

options.es: Das war der beste Tag seit Monaten!
options.en: That was the best day in months!
options.feedback: It may well have been. Said out loud at this volume it lands about three sizes too big.
